sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Regency Phase (1556-1560)**: Dominated by **Bairam Khan** (Khan-i-Khanan), who acted as the 'Vakil' and ensured the survival of the dynasty post-Humayun.
• **Second Battle of Panipat (1556)**: Decisive victory over **Hemu** (Vikramaditya), ending the Afghan-Sur threat to Delhi and Agra.
• **Petty Kingdom Consolidation**: Systematic annexation of Gwalior, Ajmer, and Jaunpur to secure the central Doab region.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: The shift from 'military occupation' to 'administrative integration' via the early Mansabdari system.

items.definition: The highest executive office during the early reign, held by Bairam Khan, acting as the de facto head of state.
A historiographical term referring to the period (1560-1562) where Akbar's foster mother Maham Anga and her son Adham Khan exerted significant influence.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Centralization**: Elimination of the 'Ataga Khail' faction to establish absolute monarchical authority.
• **Military Reform**: Introduction of the 'Dagh' (branding) system to prevent corruption in the cavalry.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Rebellion of the Uzbek nobles and the threat of Mirza Hakim from Kabul.
• **Solutions**: Strategic matrimonial alliances (Rajput policy) to neutralize regional resistance.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'P-M-G-R' (Panipat, Malwa, Garha, Rajput).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Sequence of early expansion: Panipat (1556) -> Malwa (1561) -> Garha Katanga (1564) -> Rajput Alliance (1562 onwards).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the 'Petticoat Government' with the 'Regency of Bairam Khan'. Bairam Khan was the Regent; the Petticoat Government followed his dismissal.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Imperial Consolidation' rather than just 'conquest' to describe Akbar's early phase, highlighting the shift from nomadic raiding to sedentary state-building.

keyTakeaways: The early expansion was defined by the transition from a military regency to a centralized autocracy.
The defeat of Hemu at Panipat II was the foundational event that secured the Mughal claim to the throne of Delhi.
Akbar's early policy was marked by the systematic removal of powerful regents and the establishment of direct control over the nobility.
